title: row10
live_proof: inspection with line numbers in the 3.22.0 tree: fts5StructureAddLevel() edits the Fts5Structure in place at fts5_index.c:925, and the reference count it ignores is at :339. Fixed upstream in 3.37.0. The free host ASan reports is fts5StructureExtendLevel's realloc of aSeg, not the add-level's realloc of the structure (corrected 2026-10-26 from results/2026-10-11-host-asan and results/2026-10-24-poisoncap/RESULTS.md)
object: the aSeg array of one level of the shared Fts5Structure (nRef > 1), into which the fts5vocab cursor's segment iterator points
lifetime_ender: fts5StructureExtendLevel (fts5_index.c:962, called from fts5FlushOneHash) reallocates aSeg while the cursor still reads it; host ASan reports this free and the stale read in fts5SegIterNextPage (results/2026-10-11-host-asan). Under memsys5's power-of-two rounding the array grows in place: the address stays, and the old allocation still ends (C11 7.22.3.5)
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: an fts5vocab scan cursor holding a reference, with inserts driving segment merges mid-scan. Two build constraints that are part of the case, not incidental: -DSQLITE_DQS=0 means SQL string literals must be single-quoted, and the heap stays at the 256 KiB default because raising it inflates the in-image sqlite_heap[] until the domain exceeds the buddy allocator's maximum order and DOM_CREATE fails before a single instruction runs

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect
